findings.title: False centered-proxy concentration inequality invalidates the central general-noise derivation
findings.source_claim: Each one-sided tail is bounded by exp(-2t^2/sum centered MGF proxies squared).

counterexample.assumptions: Independent bounded real input; G globally 1-Lipschitz; centered MGF proxy exactly 1/2

findings.impact: False theorem is a direct step in a central general-noise phase-transition guarantee. C.1 also fails on the intended admissible family domain as detailed in report.
findings.counterevidence: Bounded-uniform special cases can use ordinary bounded differences. Threshold phenomena and empirical curves are not refuted.
findings.repair: A verified sufficient independent-noise replacement is gamma_safe=2 L sqrt(Smax log(1/theta))/D with explicitly positive, interval-uniform quantities and admissible shifted points.
findings.repair_verification: Derived from the primary subgaussian-diameter theorem; independently checked. Original bound and dependent-noise extension not repaired automatically.

findings.title: Polynomial-profile sensitivity differentiates with respect to the wrong variable
findings.source_claim: Absolute beta derivative equals beta/(2n) sum s^(beta-1), implying a local lower bound.

counterexample.inputs: n=1; s11=0.9; beta1=1; any fixed interior second-subskill parameters; scaled uniform sigma=0.1; average aggregation

findings.impact: False local sensitivity bound is propagated into the advertised polynomial-profile transition-width derivation.
findings.counterevidence: The actual source includes absolute-value bars. The global derivative infimum can still be zero as beta tends to infinity; linear-profile conclusions are separate.
findings.repair: Correct magnitude is (1/(2n)) sum s^beta log(1/s); compact-interval minimum occurs at b_max for interior difficulties.
findings.repair_verification: Symbolic derivative and numeric check verified; width and interval self-consistency must be recomputed.

findings.status: confirmed for explicit margin-only sufficient-condition claim
findings.title: Complementary ability gaps alone do not guarantee positive merging gain
findings.location: Linear-profile illustration p.6, compared with full Theorem 3.3 p.5
findings.source_claim: Opposite ability margins of the displayed order imply gain at least 1-2theta for both original workers.

counterexample.inputs: n=m=20; each task uses all skills; average aggregation; iid Uniform[0,1] difficulties; scaled-uniform sigma=.001; theta=.1; tau=.25; W1=(.9,.8), W2=(.8,.9), merged=(.9,.9)
counterexample.assumptions: All stated linear-profile/independence/support assumptions hold; ability margins dominate exact widths on a positive-probability difficulty box and any fixed hidden constant as sigma tends to zero

findings.impact: The central explanatory sufficient condition omits the threshold position needed for a gain.
findings.counterevidence: If the full threshold sandwich is implicitly inherited, the conditional theorem survives. The finding does not refute Theorem 3.3 under all its original assumptions.
findings.repair: Restore the threshold sandwich explicitly and delimit the interpretation; concentration repair is separately necessary.
findings.repair_verification: Exact support and margin calculations checked independently; no author adoption requested.
